brief: Since 2023, equities have absorbed a sharp rise in bond yields more resiliently than history implies, helped by stronger earnings growth, AI investment and productivity optimism. With the US 10-year yield above 5%, the note asks where the valuation pain threshold sits. Repricing speed matters more than level: equity returns worsen once monthly yield changes exceed one standard deviation, worst above two, and the recent selloff has pushed repricing pace near those weak-return levels. A signal tracking the 10-year yield's position within its rolling three-year range triggers above the 90th percentile. It fired in early 2025 before that correction and has fired again. Of 18 such signals since 1964, it preceded three of the last four bear markets, and forward equity returns have historically deteriorated after triggering, though framed as a warning, not a timing tool. The estimated pain-threshold inflection is 4.5%-5.0% on the 10-year, but that relationship largely disappears once earnings growth exceeds 20%. The desk does not call a broader bear market, though a harder phase may persist into the November midterms. It expects leadership to broaden beyond AI names toward industrials, electrification, healthcare and select tech screened for positive EPS revisions, raised guidance and favorable PEG ratios.
